Figure 11 of the original SEB paper constructs dendrimers from Gaussian
polymers and thin rods. Each new generation branches from a free endpoint or
from a newly sampled contour position.

![Published Figure 11: recursively assembled polymer and rod dendrimers.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tobionecenobi/pySEB/main/PaperFigs/fig11.png){fig-alt="Published Figure 11 comparing endpoint-linked and contour-linked dendrimers assembled from Gaussian polymers and thin rods." width="90%"}

The publication uses four generations. This page executes three generations
to keep routine documentation builds responsive; changing `generations` to
four restores the published topology.

## Recursive construction

A zero-scattering `Point` supplies the root. Functionality three creates three
branches at the root and two children at every later branch: one connection is
already occupied by the branch's parent.

```{python}
import math

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pyseb


def build_dendrimer(model, link_mode, generations=3, functionality=3):
    world = pyseb.World(f"Figure11-{model}-{link_mode}")
    graph = world.Add("Point", "center")
    next_index = 0

    def attach(generation, parent_reference):
        nonlocal next_index
        child_count = (
            functionality
            if parent_reference == "center.point"
            else functionality - 1
        )

        for _ in range(child_count):
            index = next_index
            next_index += 1
            name = f"branch{index}"

            if link_mode == "ends":
                incoming = f"{name}.end1"
                outgoing = f"{name}.end2"
            else:
                incoming = f"{name}.contour#in{index}"
                outgoing = f"{name}.contour#out{index}"

            world.Link(model, incoming, parent_reference, "branch")
            if generation > 1:
                attach(generation - 1, outgoing)

    attach(generations, "center.point")
    world.Add(graph, "dendrimer")
    return world, next_index
```

The counter gives every branch a unique instance name and every distributed
contour reference a stable anchor suffix.

## Build the four comparisons

The rod length $\sqrt{12}$ and polymer radius of gyration 1 give each branch
$R_g^2=1$.

```{python}
generations = 3
specifications = [
    ("Polymer: endpoint", "GaussianPolymer", "ends",
     {"beta_branch": 1.0, "Rg_branch": 1.0}),
    ("Polymer: contour", "GaussianPolymer", "contour",
     {"beta_branch": 1.0, "Rg_branch": 1.0}),
    ("Rod: endpoint", "ThinRod", "ends",
     {"beta_branch": 1.0, "L_branch": math.sqrt(12.0)}),
    ("Rod: contour", "ThinRod", "contour",
     {"beta_branch": 1.0, "L_branch": math.sqrt(12.0)}),
]

dendrimers = {}
for label, model, mode, parameters in specifications:
    world, branch_count = build_dendrimer(model, mode, generations)
    dendrimers[label] = (world, parameters)

print(f"branches per dendrimer: {branch_count}")
```

With functionality three, the number of scattering branches is
$3 + 6 + 12 = 21$ for three generations and 45 for four generations.

## Evaluate and compare

```{python}
q = np.geomspace(1e-2, 30.0, 64)
curves = {
    label: np.asarray(
        world.EvaluateFormFactor("dendrimer", parameters, q.tolist())
    )
    for label, (world, parameters) in dendrimers.items()
}
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-figure11-dendrimer-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Three-generation polymer and rod dendrimers joined through fixed endpoints or distributed contour references."

for label, values in curves.items():
    plt.loglog(q, values, label=label)
plt.xlabel(r"$q$")
plt.ylabel(r"$F(q)$")
plt.legend(fontsize="small")
plt.show()
```

Recursion changes only the topology-building code. pySEB derives all
intra-branch and inter-branch scattering terms from the resulting graph.

## What this demonstrates

- A recursive function can grow a connected SEB graph without special
  dendrimer primitives.
- The root functionality and later functionality differ because every branch
  after the root already has a parent.
- Replacing `end1`/`end2` with distributed `contour` references changes the
  ensemble while preserving the branching topology.
- One shared tag keeps the parameter count fixed as the dendrimer grows.
